name: star_upper_gi_erefs_rings_moderate

name: star_upper_gi_erefs_exudates_mild

name: star_upper_gi_erefs_exudates_severe
description: Severe exudates observed (confluent plaques covering large areas of the esophageal mucosa)

name: star_upper_gi_forrest_III
description: Lesion without bleeding; flat spot / Clean base (Forrest III).

name: star_upper_gi_los_angeles_classification_a
description: Grade A esophagitis: One or more mucosal break ≤ 5 mm that does not extend between the tops of two mucosal folds.

name: star_upper_gi_los_angeles_classification_b
description: Grade B esophagitis: One or more mucosal break > 5 mm that does not extend between the tops of two mucosal folds.

name: star_upper_gi_los_angeles_classification_c
description: Grade C esophagitis: One or more mucosal break that is continuous between the tops of two or more mucosal folds but that involves < 75 % of the circumference.

name: star_upper_gi_los_angeles_classification_d
description: Grade D esophagitis: One or more mucosal break that involves ≥ 75 % of the esophageal circumference.

name: star_upper_gi_paris_III

name: star_upper_gi_paris_IIa_IIc

name: star_upper_gi_paris_IIc_IIa
description: Paris 0-IIc/IIa: mucosal depression with a raised edge.

name: star_upper_gi_grace_1
description: Mucus, bubbles, biliary fluid, or foam severely covers more than 50% of the surface.

name: star_upper_gi_grace_2
description: Mucus, bubbles, biliary fluid, or foam moderately covers 5% to 50% of the surface.

name: star_upper_gi_grace_3
description: No or minimal residue covers less than 5% of the surface.

name: star_upper_gi_peace_0
description: Fluid, foam, or solid content completely prevents mucosal evaluation.

name: star_upper_gi_peace_1
description: Substantial opaque content prevents evaluation of some mucosal areas.

name: star_upper_gi_peace_2
description: A small amount of hazy content permits inspection of most mucosa.

name: star_upper_gi_peace_3
description: Clean mucosa or minor transparent fluid does not impede inspection.

name: star_upper_gi_barcelona_0
description: Nonaspirable residue, bile, or foam prevents visualization of most mucosa.

name: star_upper_gi_barcelona_1
description: A small amount of residue, bile, or foam permits visualization of most mucosa.

name: star_upper_gi_barcelona_2
description: No residue is present and visualization is nearly complete.

name: star_upper_gi_stomach_varices_sarin_gov1
description: Gastroesophageal varices type 1 (GOV1) Appear as continuations of esophageal varices and extend for 2 to 5 cm below the gastroesophageal junction, along the lesser curve of the stomach.

name: star_upper_gi_stomach_varices_sarin_gov2
description: Gastroesophageal varices type 2 (GOV2) Extend beyond the gastroesophageal junction into the fundus of the stomach.

name: star_upper_gi_stomach_varices_sarin_igv1
description: Isolated gastric varices type 1 (IGV1) Are located in the fundus of the stomach and fall short of the cardia by a few centimeters.

name: star_upper_gi_stomach_varices_sarin_igv2
description: Isolated gastric varices type 2 (IGV2) Include isolated ectopic varices and can appear anywhere in the stomach, such as in the body, antrum, or pylorus.
